sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁心理学》，这是一个探讨我们在二十岁时所经历的重大生活变迁和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们还是要剖析二十岁的心理。

sentences.en: If nothing else, our 20s are this kind of beautiful time of transformation and reinvention that is a universal truth, a universal statement for me that each of us,
sentences.zh: 如果说二十岁有什么特别之处，那就是这是一个充满蜕变和重塑的美好时期，对我来说这是一个普遍真理，一个普遍的陈述，即我们每个人，

sentences.en: no matter what we're going through, what we're struggling with, what we do or don't achieve, we will have to rediscover time and time again who we are.
sentences.zh: 无论我们正在经历什么，无论我们在为什么而挣扎，无论我们取得了什么成就或未取得什么成就，我们都将不得不一次又一次地重新发现自己是谁。

sentences.en: And we also have to rediscover how far off that is from who we want to be probably hundreds of times during this period of emerging adulthood.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个新兴成年期的过程中，我们可能还要数百次地重新发现自己与理想中的自我之间还有多大的差距。

sentences.en: We spend so much of childhood and also our teenage years being the person that others want us to be
sentences.zh: 我们花了很多童年和青少年时期去成为别人希望我们成为的人，

sentences.en: or rebelling against this version entirely to carve out what we think is our own space.
sentences.zh: 或者完全反叛这种设定，去开辟我们认为属于自己的空间。

sentences.en: And I think our 20s is when we start to find balance and we really get the chance to do that all over again
sentences.zh: 我认为二十岁是我们开始寻找平衡的时候，我们真的有机会重新来过，

sentences.en: and independently and we approach, you know, self-discovery with a new maturity and a new sense of truth.
sentences.zh: 并且是独立地，我们以一种新的成熟度和新的真实感来对待自我发现。

sentences.en: Things about us become a lot more clear.
sentences.zh: 关于我们自己的事情变得清晰多了。

sentences.en: And what we're likely to experience is a bit of a metamorphosis and a shedding of the old into the new.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会经历某种蜕变，抛弃旧我，迎来新我。

sentences.en: This is definitely a rite of passage and sometimes it's deeply uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一种成人礼，有时会让人感到非常不适。

sentences.en: But when you get to the point of not really enjoying your life, not liking who you are, not knowing what you stand for, what your dreams are, who you even want to be,
sentences.zh: 但当你发现自己不再享受生活，不喜欢现在的自己，不知道自己坚持什么，不知道梦想是什么，甚至不知道自己想成为什么样的人时，

sentences.en: you are really, I think, called to a place of reinvention.
sentences.zh: 我认为你真的被召唤到了一个需要重塑自我的境地。

sentences.en: And that is what I want to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我今天想谈论的话题。

sentences.en: How can we reinvent and rediscover ourselves in our 20s when things start to feel stagnant or off or we start to feel a sense of disconnection between who we are right now
sentences.zh: 当我们二十岁时，当事情开始感到停滞、不对劲，或者我们开始感到现在的自己与真正想成为的自己之间存在某种脱节时，我们该如何重塑和重新发现自己？

sentences.en: and who we really want to be?
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: How do we kind of shake things up?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何打破现状？

sentences.en: How do we find our path?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何找到自己的道路？

sentences.en: How do we have that refresh where we fall back in love with our lives through our old actions?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何通过旧有的行动来重新爱上我们的生活，实现那种焕然一新？

sentences.en: Well, we are going to talk through five tips that you can work through either step by step or you can kind of choose one or the other for reinvention during this decade.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们将讨论五个技巧，你可以一步步实践，或者选择其中一个来在这个十年里重塑自我。

sentences.en: This includes some methods for visualizing your next chapter and how to use psychology to really motivate yourself to get there,
sentences.zh: 这包括一些可视化下一篇章的方法，以及如何利用心理学来真正激励自己实现目标，

sentences.en: how to use psychology to motivate a sense of confidence.
sentences.zh: 如何利用心理学来激发自信心。

sentences.en: Also how we can use that discomfort, use the boredom, the isolation, the stagnation, the uncertainty in our favor rather than fighting against it.
sentences.zh: 还有我们如何利用那种不适感，利用无聊、孤独、停滞、不确定性来为我们所用，而不是与它们对抗。

sentences.en: How can we actually take all of those things that are making us crave reinvention
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能真正利用所有那些让我们渴望重塑自我的因素，

sentences.en: and help us get there rather than kind of, I don't know, burden us?
sentences.zh: 并帮助我们到达目的地，而不是让它们成为我们的负担？

sentences.en: We are also going to discuss the power of risk and this construct called the timeline for change
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论风险的力量，以及一个叫做“变革时间轴”的概念，

sentences.en: and how to shift from very anxious what-if thinking to a what-else or so-what mentality, which is honestly one of my favorite ways to think about this.
sentences.zh: 以及如何从焦虑的“万一怎么办”思维转变为“那又怎样”或“还有什么”的心态，这老实说是我最喜欢的思考方式之一。

sentences.en: One of my favorite ideas in this space is that switch, that mental and cognitive switch from seeing things in a disaster scenario lens or from a disaster scenario lens
sentences.zh: 在这个领域，我最喜欢的想法之一就是那种转变，那种从灾难性视角看待事物的心理和认知转换，

sentences.en: to an abundant lens, from an abundant position of excess and authenticity and growth.
sentences.zh: 转变为一种丰盛的视角，一种基于富足、真实和成长的立场。

sentences.en: I've got to say this is one of my favorite episodes that I've done as of recent because it just combines all my favorite like nuggets of advice and theories into one package
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这是我最近做的最喜欢的节目之一，因为它把我所有最喜欢的建议和理论精华结合在了一起，

sentences.en: and truly it really represents so much of my philosophy towards this period in our lives.
sentences.zh: 它确实代表了我对人生这一阶段的很多哲学思考。

sentences.en: You know, our 20s are for exploration.
sentences.zh: 你知道，二十岁是用来探索的。

sentences.en: They are for reinvention, rebuilding, transformation more so than any other time.
sentences.zh: 它们比任何其他时期都更适合重塑、重建和蜕变。

sentences.en: So I really want us to be able to unlock that for ourselves, even if it's through small steps, even if it's not as drastic as you're picturing.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望我们能为自己开启这种可能，即使是通过小步骤，即使它不像你想象的那么剧烈。

sentences.en: Also, I guess whenever I get the opportunity to talk about risk and our approach to uncertainty,
sentences.zh: 另外，我想每当我有机会谈论风险和我们对待不确定性的态度时，

sentences.en: that is like a favorite topic of mine because it's something that I deeply, deeply think is important that we stop seeing risk as scary and we start seeing risk as investment.
sentences.zh: 那都是我最喜欢的话题，因为我深信我们必须停止将风险视为可怕的事物，而应将其视为一种投资。

sentences.en: It really falls into this overall concept and topic of reinvention.
sentences.zh: 这确实属于重塑自我的整体概念和主题。

sentences.en: So I am very excited to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常兴奋能谈论这个话题。

sentences.en: I'm enthused.
sentences.zh: 我充满热情。

sentences.en: I'm invigorated.
sentences.zh: 我感到精神振奋。

sentences.en: So I think without further ado, let us get into the five ways that we can reinvent ourselves in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 所以我想废话不多说，让我们进入在二十岁重塑自我的五种方法。

sentences.en: Reinventing yourself, changing your life.
sentences.zh: 重塑自我，改变生活。

sentences.en: I think it really has to begin with identifying what it is about your current circumstances, your day to day, your habits that are dissatisfying to you.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的必须从识别你当前的环境、日常习惯中哪些让你感到不满开始。

sentences.en: What is the main feeling that you have towards your life at the moment that is giving you this itch to change things up that is making you restless?
sentences.zh: 你此刻对生活的主要感受是什么？是什么让你产生了想要改变现状的冲动，让你感到不安？

sentences.en: There are a few big ones that I think are specifically noteworthy in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我认为在二十岁时有几个特别值得注意的大问题。

sentences.en: The first one is boredom.
sentences.zh: 第一个是无聊。

sentences.en: Boredom, feeling like not much is happening in your life.
sentences.zh: 无聊，感觉生活中没发生什么事。

sentences.en: Nothing exciting is happening.
sentences.zh: 没什么令人兴奋的事情发生。

sentences.en: Nothing is changing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: You're not changing the things that really elevate our day to day experiences like adventure, like excitement, like spontaneity.
sentences.zh: 你没有改变那些真正提升我们日常体验的事情，比如冒险、兴奋、自发性。

sentences.en: It's just not there.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不存在。

sentences.en: It's this sense of just like plainness.
sentences.zh: 这是一种平淡无奇的感觉。

sentences.en: Boredom is the first one.
sentences.zh: 无聊是第一个。

sentences.en: Then we have stagnation.
sentences.zh: 然后是停滞。

sentences.en: And this is very similar to boredom.
sentences.zh: 这和无聊非常相似。

sentences.en: But it's more so centered on a sense that you've kind of become complacent in some domain of your life, even if you're still doing fun things.
sentences.zh: 但它更多地集中于一种感觉，即你在生活的某个领域变得自满了，即使你还在做一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: This is particularly to do with our careers or to do with some larger goal, finding that, you know, you're really not working towards something the way that you anticipated that
sentences.zh: 这特别与我们的职业生涯或某些更大的目标有关，发现你并没有像预期的那样朝着某个目标努力，

sentences.en: you would be or the way that you have in the past, feeling very stuck.
sentences.zh: 或者不像过去那样，感觉非常被困住了。

sentences.en: Then we have isolation, lacking connection, lacking community, feeling lonely.
sentences.zh: 然后是孤独，缺乏联系，缺乏社区，感到寂寞。

sentences.en: And maybe with that, you know, some FOMO that you're missing out on the experiences that others seem to be having during this time.
sentences.zh: 也许随之而来的是某种错失恐惧症（FOMO），觉得你错过了别人在这个时期似乎正在经历的体验。

sentences.en: And then the final feeling that I think also makes us quite itchy for change is just a general
sentences.zh: 最后一种感觉，我认为也让我们非常渴望改变，那就是一种普遍的

sentences.en: discomfort, a feeling that's probably very similar to anxiety, that something about your life just isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 不适感，一种可能与焦虑非常相似的感觉，即你的生活中有某些东西不太对劲。

sentences.en: You don't seem to fit in your current circumstances anymore.
sentences.zh: 你似乎不再适合你当前的环境了。

sentences.en: You know, you have these habits, these friends, these situations that your body is very instinctually telling you this is not what we want.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你有这些习惯、这些朋友、这些处境，你的身体本能地告诉你，这不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: We're not comfortable here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不舒服。

sentences.en: We're not happy here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不快乐。

sentences.en: And often it does that through heightened sensitivity, being very nervous, repetitive thoughts that
sentences.zh: 通常它通过高度敏感、非常紧张、重复的思维来表现，

sentences.en: again and again bring you back to some issue that you're having, a sense of detachment between who you know you can be and who you are now.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次地把你带回你正在面临的某个问题，一种你知道自己可以成为的样子与现在的你之间的脱节感。

sentences.en: So these feelings, boredom, stagnation, isolation and discomfort, they tell us something very useful, even though it's unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 所以这些感觉——无聊、停滞、孤独和不适——告诉了我们一些非常有用的东西，尽管它们令人不快。

sentences.en: And what they're telling us is that we need to change.
sentences.zh: 它们告诉我们的是，我们需要改变。

sentences.en: We need to shift.
sentences.zh: 我们需要转变。

sentences.en: We need to be doing something different and hopefully sooner rather than later.
sentences.zh: 我们需要做一些不同的事情，而且希望越快越好。

sentences.en: The reason that I say sooner rather than later is because if you don't do something not instantly, but
sentences.zh: 我之所以说越快越好，是因为如果你不立刻做点什么，

sentences.en: pretty soon, the alternative is that we begin to get quite comfortable with the discomfort.
sentences.zh: 很快，另一种选择就是我们开始习惯这种不适。

sentences.en: We get comfortable with being bored, with being lonely, with being stuck, and we think that that's normal.
sentences.zh: 我们习惯了无聊、孤独、被困住，并认为这是正常的。

sentences.en: In psychology, this process is actually called habituation, and it refers to our tendency to
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，这个过程实际上被称为“习惯化”，它指的是我们倾向于

sentences.en: get more and more used to something that used to frustrate us or bother us as time goes on.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，对那些曾经让我们沮丧或困扰的事情变得越来越习以为常。

sentences.en: You know, I think about, so I, for example, I actually live under like a plane line.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想到了，比如我，我实际上住在飞机航线下面。

sentences.en: What's it called?
sentences.zh: 那叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Like a flight path, right?
sentences.zh: 就像飞行航线一样，对吧？

sentences.en: And when I first moved into this house, like the sound of planes going overhead was so, would just bother me so much.
sentences.zh: 我刚搬进这栋房子时，头顶上飞机的轰鸣声真的让我非常困扰。

sentences.en: It was all I could think about.
sentences.zh: 我满脑子想的都是这个。

sentences.en: But the longer that I've lived here, I don't even notice it anymore.
sentences.zh: 但住得越久，我甚至都察觉不到它的存在了。

sentences.en: Like I'm sure that about five planes have probably flown over the skies above my house in the time that I've been recording this.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，在我录制这段音频的时间里，大概已经有五架飞机从我家上空飞过了。

sentences.en: But I've become habituated, and that is the same thing that happens when we get comfortable with something that we should not be comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 但我已经习惯了，当我们对某些本不该习以为常的事情感到安逸时，也会发生同样的情况。

sentences.en: You should not be comfortable with being bored in your life, or being isolated, or being, you know, stagnant.
sentences.zh: 你不应该对生活中的无聊、孤立，或者说停滞不前感到安逸。

sentences.en: And we have a really small window to stop that habituation from happening and to act.
sentences.zh: 我们只有很短的时间窗口来阻止这种习惯化，并采取行动。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it does get harder and harder.
sentences.zh: 否则，事情只会变得越来越难。

sentences.en: It's like breaking a bad habit.
sentences.zh: 这就像戒掉坏习惯一样。

sentences.en: What we want to explore is what life would look like if we flipped those emotional states to be the complete opposite.
sentences.zh: 我们想探讨的是，如果我们把这些情绪状态完全反转过来，生活会是什么样子。

sentences.en: So when we felt bored, we made a commitment to pursue excitement.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们感到无聊时，我们承诺去追求刺激。

sentences.en: When we felt stagnant, we made a commitment to pursue growth, to pursue connection over isolation, to pursue peace and boundaries over discomfort.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到停滞时，我们承诺去追求成长，用连接取代孤立，用平静和界限取代不适。

sentences.en: So what I want from you is to really, to begin with, notice what is driving you to want to
sentences.zh: 所以，我希望你首先要做的，是去留意是什么在驱使你想要

sentences.en: reinvent or refresh your life, and then make a plan for the next 30 days to do all the things that feel the exact opposite to that initial feeling.
sentences.zh: 重塑或焕新你的生活，然后制定一个未来30天的计划，去做所有与那种最初感受截然相反的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to really shake up your life whilst you're still feeling motivated by the discomfort.
sentences.zh: 趁着你还被这种不适感所激励，我们要彻底改变你的生活。

sentences.en: For example, if you are just feeling so bored with your life right now, I want you to make
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你现在对生活感到非常无聊，我希望你能在

sentences.en: a list in your notes up or on a sheet of paper to put on your fridge of a series of activities that you've always wanted to do in your city or your town that you haven't.
sentences.zh: 笔记里或纸上列出一系列你一直想在所在的城市或小镇做却还没做过的事情，然后把清单贴在冰箱上。

sentences.en: And I want you to be committed to doing one every two days, every three days.
sentences.zh: 我希望你承诺每两三天就去完成其中一件。

sentences.en: Or if there is a class, a hobby you've always wanted to pursue, sign up for a six-week course
sentences.zh: 或者，如果有什么课程或爱好是你一直想尝试的，那就报名参加一个六周的课程，

sentences.en: that you have to go to week after a week, get a new gym membership, just do something different.
sentences.zh: 你需要每周都去上课，或者办一张新的健身卡，总之做点不一样的事情。

sentences.en: Novel experiences quite literally give the impression of creating more time in our lives.
sentences.zh: 新奇的体验确实能给人一种让生命变得更漫长的感觉。

sentences.en: And there's a 2016 study around this that has become quite well known that found that the older we get, time does seem to actually pass quicker.
sentences.zh: 2016年有一项关于此的研究非常出名，它发现随着年龄增长，时间似乎确实过得更快了。

sentences.en: Not because it's actually going any faster, but because we are learning less.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为时间真的变快了，而是因为我们学到的东西变少了。

sentences.en: We are exposed to fewer new things.
sentences.zh: 我们接触的新鲜事物变少了。

sentences.en: We become more accustomed to what we already know.
sentences.zh: 我们对已知的事物变得更加习以为常。

sentences.en: But what actually creates the mental experience of more time is novelty and newness.
sentences.zh: 但真正创造出“时间变多”这种心理体验的，是新奇感和新鲜感。

sentences.en: And that is what we need to reintroduce to kind of pull us out of the path towards indifference and monotony.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们需要重新引入的东西，以将我们从通往冷漠和单调的道路上拉回来。

sentences.en: So put the excitement back in your life because that is a choice for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，让兴奋感回归你的生活吧，因为这是一种选择。

sentences.en: You know, that is something that you can change on your own to reinvent how you feel about your circumstances.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是你可以自己改变的事情，从而重塑你对自身处境的感受。

sentences.en: The same goes for if you're feeling stagnant.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到停滞不前，道理也是一样的。

sentences.en: You know, identify what area that's in and make yourself a list of a series of things that you know would help you break out of that.
sentences.zh: 找出停滞的领域，列出一系列你知道能帮你打破现状的事情。

sentences.en: If it's work related, which I find it often is, or career related, I want you to change your routine.
sentences.zh: 如果是工作或职业相关的问题——我发现通常都是这样——我希望你改变你的日常惯例。

sentences.en: I want you to spend 30 minutes a day applying for new jobs instead of scrolling.
sentences.zh: 我希望你每天花30分钟申请新工作，而不是刷手机。

sentences.en: I want you to be networking.
sentences.zh: 我希望你去建立人脉。

sentences.en: I want you to be, you know, reaching out to people that you admire online, shooting off those emails so that when you go to bed, you have a sense that you've done something.
sentences.zh: 我希望你去联系那些你在网上钦佩的人，发出那些邮件，这样当你上床睡觉时，你会有一种自己有所作为的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, sign up for the networking event.
sentences.zh: 去报名参加社交活动吧。

sentences.en: Contemplate what you could do next.
sentences.zh: 思考一下你接下来能做什么。

sentences.en: I think reinvention is all about movement and picking the direction you want to go in and actually pursuing it.
sentences.zh: 我认为重塑的核心在于行动，在于选定你想去的方向并真正去追求它。

sentences.en: Once you've kind of tested sliding the dial to your boredom, your stagnation, whatever it is in the opposite direction, it's time to really begin to visualize your next era
sentences.zh: 一旦你尝试过将生活的指针向无聊、停滞等状态的反方向拨动，就是时候开始构想你的下一个阶段了，

sentences.en: and who this new version of you will be, but also how this new version of you will act.
sentences.zh: 构想这个新版本的你将是谁，以及这个新版本的你将如何行动。

sentences.en: You know, in your wildest fantasies, your greatest, largest dreams, who is your authentic self?
sentences.zh: 在最狂野的幻想和最宏大的梦想中，你真实的自我究竟是谁？

sentences.en: Who is the character staring back at you?
sentences.zh: 那个回望你的角色是谁？

sentences.en: If you still are unsure about who that is, how to even visualize this version of yourself, I have some questions to really help you bring elements of this person forward.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不确定那个人是谁，甚至不知道如何构想这个版本的自己，我有一些问题可以帮你把这个人的特质挖掘出来。

sentences.en: So what are some of the dreams that you've had for as long as you can remember that you've always put off?
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些梦想是你从记事起就一直有，却总是推迟去实现的？

sentences.en: What truly excites you?
sentences.zh: 什么真正让你感到兴奋？

sentences.en: What could you talk about for hours?
sentences.zh: 什么话题是你能够滔滔不绝聊上几个小时的？

sentences.en: In five years time, what would your ideal but average day in your life look like?
sentences.zh: 五年后，你理想中但平凡的一天会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And how is that different from now?
sentences.zh: 那与现在有什么不同？

sentences.en: What chapter of your life are you ready to close?
sentences.zh: 你准备好翻过人生的哪一章了？

sentences.en: And what is holding you back from closing that chapter?
sentences.zh: 是什么在阻碍你翻过那一章？

sentences.en: Or what is holding you back from putting everything behind the truest version of yourself?
sentences.zh: 或者说，是什么在阻碍你全力支持那个最真实的自己？

sentences.en: Your answers to these questions should really begin to direct you to what this next era of your life is going to bring.
sentences.zh: 你对这些问题的回答，应该能开始指引你走向人生的下一个阶段。

sentences.en: You know, if you were to look back, I think, and if we were to look back at past versions,
sentences.zh: 如果你回首往事，我想，如果我们回首过去版本的自己，

sentences.en: you know, past parts of our life story, you start to really see in hindsight these strange lines or periods that are carved into your memories.
sentences.zh: 回首人生故事的过去片段，你开始真正从后见之明中看到那些刻在记忆里的奇怪线条或时期。

sentences.en: You begin to notice that life isn't one long sequence of events.
sentences.zh: 你开始注意到，生活并不是一连串漫长的事件。

sentences.en: And I guess it is, but actually it's a series of seasons and a series of periods within which
sentences.zh: 我想它确实是，但实际上它是一系列季节和时期，在这些时期里，

sentences.en: you've had different goals, maybe different friends, different ambitions, different, you know, sense of style.
sentences.zh: 你有不同的目标，可能还有不同的朋友、不同的抱负、不同的审美风格。

sentences.en: You maybe you've even lived in a different place.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能住在不同的地方。

sentences.en: Your routine was different.
sentences.zh: 你的日常惯例也不同。

sentences.en: We each have these different eras or chapters of our lives that represent who we were and what we were going through at that time.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都有这些不同的人生阶段或篇章，代表了我们当时是谁以及正在经历什么。

sentences.en: And this next era for you is going to be one of authenticity.
sentences.zh: 而你的下一个阶段将是关于“真实”的。

sentences.en: It's going to be one where you're going to channel all of those deeply rooted dreams and values and goals and actually just spend the next six months to a year prioritizing them.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你将引导所有那些深植于心的梦想、价值观和目标，并真正花上六个月到一年的时间去优先考虑它们。

sentences.en: That is how you're going to bring yourself into this next chapter and reinvent yourself.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何进入下一个篇章并重塑自我的方式。

sentences.en: We can be in the business of deciding when a new season begins for us, regardless of what is happening externally.
sentences.zh: 无论外界发生什么，我们都可以主动决定何时开启人生的新篇章。

sentences.en: And that really starts with being able to see, feel, touch, hear, experience what this new era represents for you before it even emerges.
sentences.zh: 这始于你能够在这一新阶段到来之前，就先看到、感觉到、触碰到、听到并体验到它所代表的意义。

sentences.en: And you've already done that in a way by focusing on those questions that we were talking about before.
sentences.zh: 通过专注于我们之前讨论的那些问题，你已经在某种程度上做到了这一点。

sentences.en: You do already have an idea, but then you have to get it out of your mind into some physical form, either through action or through something like visualization.
sentences.zh: 你已经有了想法，但你必须将其从脑海中提取出来，转化为某种物理形式，无论是通过行动还是通过可视化之类的手段。

sentences.en: So some ways that people do this is through like vision boards, you know, spending an afternoon
sentences.zh: 人们实现这一点的方法之一是制作愿景板，花一个下午的时间，

sentences.en: really putting to page or to poster what this next chapter looks like for you, you know, with
sentences.zh: 真正把这个新篇章的样子写在纸上或贴在海报上，

sentences.en: pictures of destinations that you'll visit and accomplishments and the nature that you'll see, the mornings that you'll have, the hobbies that will relax you.
sentences.zh: 配上你想去的目的地、想达成的成就、想欣赏的自然风光、想拥有的清晨，以及让你放松的爱好的图片。

sentences.en: You need to have an idea of what you're actually aiming for here.
sentences.zh: 你需要对自己真正追求的目标有一个清晰的概念。

sentences.en: And visualization is extremely psychologically powerful.
sentences.zh: 可视化在心理学上是非常强大的。

sentences.en: There was a recent study that said about a quarter of successful entrepreneurs use vision boards or a similar process to map out change for themselves.
sentences.zh: 最近有一项研究表明，大约四分之一的成功企业家使用愿景板或类似的过程来规划自己的变革。

sentences.en: And there was a 2019 study that also suggests that vision boards, as much as we sometimes think
sentences.zh: 2019年还有一项研究表明，尽管我们有时认为愿景板很傻，但实际上，

sentences.en: that they're silly, actually, no, they almost double an individual's level of confidence in their ability to effectively execute actions necessary to achieve a desired outcome.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎能使个人在有效执行实现预期结果所需行动方面的自信心翻倍。

sentences.en: And it really promotes people to seek out supportive resources.
sentences.zh: 它确实能促进人们去寻求支持性资源。

sentences.en: And it keeps this vision of who they want to be, who they're working towards very squarely in the front of their mind.
sentences.zh: 它让人们想要成为什么样的人、正在努力实现什么目标的愿景，始终清晰地呈现在脑海中。

sentences.en: Because life is full of distractions.
sentences.zh: 因为生活中充满了干扰。

sentences.en: There are lots of things pulling us this way, that way.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情在把我们拉向这个或那个方向。

sentences.en: You know, you're busy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你很忙。

sentences.en: You know, there's people's expectations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有来自他人的期望。

sentences.en: There's money to worry about.
sentences.zh: 有金钱方面的担忧。

sentences.en: There's, you know, relationships to worry about.
sentences.zh: 有需要操心的人际关系。

sentences.en: But this method really squarely says, very deeply says, no, this is what we're working towards right now.
sentences.zh: 但这种方法非常明确地、深刻地告诉你：不，这就是我们现在努力的方向。

sentences.en: This is who we want to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们想要成为的人。

sentences.en: Another way to do this, if visualization and, you know, mood boards, vision boards, sorry, aren't really your favorite method, it's to identify a theme for your new era that you
sentences.zh: 如果你不喜欢可视化、情绪板或愿景板，另一种方法是为你的新阶段确定一个主题，

sentences.en: really want to embody and that you will use to charge, motivate, direct everything that you're doing in this new season.
sentences.zh: 一个你真正想要体现的主题，并用它来激励、指引你在新阶段所做的一切。

sentences.en: As in, you know, when it's time to make a decision or you have a hard choice ahead of you,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当需要做决定或面临艰难选择时，

sentences.en: I want you to have that one theme, that one word that decisively chooses for you.
sentences.zh: 我希望你拥有那个主题，那个能为你做出果断选择的词。

sentences.en: Let me explain this a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 让我再多解释一下。

sentences.en: So with this new era, your theme could be discipline.
sentences.zh: 在这个新阶段，你的主题可以是“自律”。

sentences.en: It could be reinvention, rebirth, passion, creativity, authenticity, exploration, intuition, focus, courage.
sentences.zh: 也可以是“重塑”、“重生”、“激情”、“创造力”、“真实”、“探索”、“直觉”、“专注”或“勇气”。

sentences.en: I want you to choose one of those or one of your own.
sentences.zh: 我希望你从中选择一个，或者选择你自己的主题。

sentences.en: A theme that is going to sit at the core of everything you aim to do for the next six months.
sentences.zh: 这个主题将成为你未来六个月所做一切的核心。

sentences.en: Let me use the theme of reinvention here to explain why this works.
sentences.zh: 让我用“重塑”这个主题来解释为什么这行得通。

sentences.en: You know, it's very appropriate for this episode, but to embody reinvention, that really means doing things differently, right?
sentences.zh: 这对于本期节目非常贴切，但要体现“重塑”，意味着要以不同的方式做事，对吧？

sentences.en: Making space for what's new, making space for things that you haven't tried before, maybe
sentences.zh: 为新事物腾出空间，为那些你从未尝试过的事情腾出空间，也许

sentences.en: because you're scared, you're embarrassed, you're held back by the judgments of others, but you're going to do it anyways.
sentences.zh: 是因为你害怕、尴尬，或者受制于他人的评价，但你依然要去做。

sentences.en: You are stepping into this new era, you're reinventing yourself.
sentences.zh: 你正在步入这个新阶段，你正在重塑自我。

sentences.en: And I want you to seriously try and rebut my reasons with the reasons why you shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我希望你认真尝试反驳我的理由，列出你不该冒险的原因。

sentences.en: Number one, you will never have as few responsibilities as you do now.
sentences.zh: 第一，你永远不会像现在这样责任负担这么轻。

sentences.en: Number two, you are the youngest that you will ever be, probably with the least to lose.
sentences.zh: 第二，这是你一生中最年轻的时候，可能也是失去最少的时候。

sentences.en: You will never have more time than you have right now.
sentences.zh: 你永远不会拥有比现在更多的时间。

sentences.en: I also think that risks are an investment.
sentences.zh: 我也认为风险是一种投资。

sentences.en: They are not a coSt.
sentences.zh: 它们不是成本。

sentences.en: They will benefit your life and your foundations way more than the risks that you don't take and way more than playing it safe.
sentences.zh: 它们对你生活和基础的益处，远胜于你不去冒险，也远胜于求稳。

sentences.en: And finally, in a very similar vein, you are more likely to live with regret over the risks you didn't take over the ones that you did.
sentences.zh: 最后，同样道理，你更有可能因为没冒的险而后悔，而不是因为冒了险而后悔。

sentences.en: And if you want some anecdotal primary evidence of this, ask your parents or your grandparents next time you see them what their biggest regrets are.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要一些轶事作为主要证据，下次见到父母或祖父母时，问问他们最大的遗憾是什么。

sentences.en: And I would say 80% of the time, your parents are going to say, oh, you know, the time I didn't travel, the time I was too scared to do that thing that I should have, the time
sentences.zh: 我会说80%的情况下，你的父母会说，哦，你知道，我没去旅行的那次，我太害怕而没做那件我本该做的事的那次，我

sentences.en: that I didn't tell that person I loved them, the time that I said no to an opportunity that I really actually should have taken because of imposter syndrome.
sentences.zh: 没告诉那个人我爱他们的那次，因为冒名顶替综合症而拒绝了一个我本该抓住的机会的那次。

sentences.en: Regret often feeds off inaction rather than action.
sentences.zh: 遗憾往往源于不作为，而非行动。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于。

sentences.en: Reinventing yourself through risk doesn't have to be dramatic.
sentences.zh: 通过冒险来重塑自我并不一定要轰轰烈烈。

sentences.en: Some of us get really paralyzed by this idea that to move forward, we have to do something we are deeply uncertain of.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人被这种想法彻底瘫痪了：为了前进，我们必须做一些我们极其不确定的事情。

sentences.en: And normally this is the case if you're quite risk averse, right?
sentences.zh: 通常如果你比较厌恶风险，情况就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: So in psychology and economics, even there are these different profiles of the types of people and their perspective on risk.
sentences.zh: 所以在心理学和经济学中，甚至有关于人们类型及其风险观点的不同分析。

sentences.en: There are risk positive people, people who will put it all on the line very frequently without really considering the coSt.
sentences.zh: 有风险偏好型的人，他们经常把一切押上，而不真正考虑成本。

sentences.en: There are risk neutral people, people who are very practical, almost mathematical about the costs and benefits of a risk.
sentences.zh: 有风险中立型的人，他们非常务实，几乎是数学化地看待风险的成本和收益。

sentences.en: And then there are risk averse individuals, those of us whose minds just naturally exaggerate the consequences and the cost of the risk over the benefits to the point where the
sentences.zh: 还有风险厌恶型的人，我们这些人的大脑会自然地夸大风险的后果和成本，超过其收益，以至于

sentences.en: risk actually seems entirely ridiculous, you know, and we are convinced that we should always play it safe.
sentences.zh: 风险看起来完全荒谬，你知道，我们确信自己应该总是求稳。

sentences.en: And if that is you, if the idea of moving to a new country knowing no one, quitting your job without anything lined up, if that is really, really scary, what I want you to adopt
sentences.zh: 如果这就是你，如果搬到一个不认识任何人的新国家、在没有任何准备的情况下辞职，如果这些真的非常、非常可怕，我想让你采纳的

sentences.en: is this idea of micro risks, things that you can slowly incorporate to almost increase your tolerance for the uncertainty that comes along with these decisions.
sentences.zh: 是这种“微风险”的概念，你可以慢慢融入这些事情，以增加你对这些决定所带来的不确定性的容忍度。

sentences.en: You can go on solo dates.
sentences.zh: 你可以尝试独自约会。

sentences.en: You can go on micro adventures on the weekend solo.
sentences.zh: 你可以在周末进行独自的微探险。

sentences.en: You don't have to travel across the world.
sentences.zh: 你不必非要环游世界。

sentences.en: You can book an Airbnb for the weekend in the mountains, near a national park, somewhere like an hour or two away and just enjoy a new part of the world alone.
sentences.zh: 你可以在周末预订一个山里或国家公园附近的爱彼迎，离家一两个小时的地方，独自享受世界的一个新角落。

sentences.en: My cousin Stella, actually, she was just messaging me about her solo camping trip that she's been on for the last two to three days.
sentences.zh: 其实我表妹斯特拉，她刚才还在给我发信息，说她过去两三天一直在进行独自露营旅行。

sentences.en: Literally, she's only like an hour or two from her home, but she's just having the most amazing time and she's doing something that she may not normally do.
sentences.zh: 实际上，她离家只有一两个小时的路程，但她玩得非常开心，她在做一些她平时可能不会做的事情。

sentences.en: And it's just completely expanded her perspective on her life, like in the span of two days, just getting out of an old environment and into a new one.
sentences.zh: 这完全拓宽了她对生活的视角，仅仅在两天之内，离开旧环境进入一个新环境。

sentences.en: These are small but mighty choices.
sentences.zh: 这些是微小但强大的选择。

sentences.en: Some more examples, you know, share your passion, your art, your hobbies, your lifestyle online to a private audience.
sentences.zh: 再举几个例子，你知道，在私密受众面前分享你的热情、艺术、爱好、生活方式。

sentences.en: Ask new people to go for coffee, be spontaneous, do something different this weekend that's not your usual Sunday reset.
sentences.zh: 邀请新朋友去喝咖啡，保持自发性，这个周末做点不同的事情，而不是你通常的周日重置。

sentences.en: Start putting $20 a week aside purely for a dream fund.
sentences.zh: 开始每周存20美元，专门作为梦想基金。

sentences.en: Just take, you know, those first steps without worrying about them being perfect.
sentences.zh: 只需迈出那些第一步，而不必担心它们是否完美。

sentences.en: And that might not sound like a risky thing to do for some people, but I think anything that goes against the habits, the systems, the routines that you have in place to keep
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这听起来可能不是什么冒险的事，但我认为任何违背你为了保持

sentences.en: you secure and safe that you are using as a crutch, anything that's like that, that is a risk.
sentences.zh: 安全感而建立的习惯、系统、常规，任何你当作拐杖的东西，任何类似的事情，那都是一种风险。

sentences.en: That is a risk that you are taking to go against what your natural, deeply ingrained intuition is telling you to do.
sentences.zh: 那是你为了违背你内心深处根深蒂固的直觉而冒的险。

sentences.en: What I want you to remember is that you are in charge here of creating a reality you love, creating a version of yourself that you love even more.
sentences.zh: 我想让你记住的是，你负责创造你热爱的现实，创造一个你更热爱的自己。

sentences.en: Sometimes that's going to take courage.
sentences.zh: 有时这需要勇气。

sentences.en: The path to reinvention, I think, involves risk and it involves a little bit of fear.
sentences.zh: 我认为，重塑之路涉及风险，也涉及一点恐惧。

sentences.en: So my fifth and my final tip for you today is to stop asking yourself what if and instead replace that with what else or my favorite, so what?
sentences.zh: 所以，今天给你的第五个也是最后一个建议是：停止问自己“如果……怎么办”，取而代之的是“还有什么”或者我最喜欢的“那又怎样”。

sentences.en: Each of us again has an idea of our truest selves, the person that we would be if no one else was watching.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人再次拥有一个关于最真实自我的想法，即如果没人注视，我们会成为的那个人。

sentences.en: If this magical switch was turned that suddenly meant that you were free from others' opinions.
sentences.zh: 如果这个神奇的开关被打开，突然意味着你从他人的意见中解脱出来。

sentences.en: If the only person we were focused on was ourselves.
sentences.zh: 如果我们唯一关注的人就是我们自己。

sentences.en: We all had this idea of who we would be in that situation.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们都有一个关于自己会成为谁的想法。

sentences.en: They're almost a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎是一种幻想。

sentences.en: They're a character, you know, that we've created that we one day aspire to be, but we're not really not really focused on that right now.
sentences.zh: 它们是一个角色，你知道，我们创造的那个我们渴望有一天能成为的人，但我们现在并没有真正关注这一点。

sentences.en: Now, the things that are really maintaining that gap between who we are now and who we would really love to be is normally our fear of judgment, our fear of upsetting others and
sentences.zh: 现在，真正维持我们现状与我们真正渴望成为的人之间差距的，通常是我们对评判的恐惧、对让别人失望和

sentences.en: their expectations, our fear of embarrassment of being perceived.
sentences.zh: 辜负他们期望的恐惧、对被关注而感到尴尬的恐惧。

sentences.en: That's a huge one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的恐惧。

sentences.en: And our fear of change.
sentences.zh: 还有我们对改变的恐惧。

sentences.en: These fears are all maintained by these what if disaster scenarios.
sentences.zh: 这些恐惧都是由这些“如果……怎么办”的灾难场景所维持的。

sentences.en: If I start putting myself out there, if I start being loud about my hobbies, about my desires,
sentences.zh: 如果我开始展示自己，如果我开始大声谈论我的爱好、我的欲望，

sentences.en: if I start wearing what I want, if I start saying no to people, if I let myself be perceived as my truest authentic self, what if no one likes this version of me?
sentences.zh: 如果我开始穿我想穿的衣服，如果我开始对别人说不，如果我让自己以最真实的自我被感知，如果没人喜欢这个版本的我怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I'm ostracized?
sentences.zh: 如果我被排斥怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I tell someone about my dreams and I fail?
sentences.zh: 如果我告诉别人我的梦想却失败了怎么办？

sentences.en: What if people don't like this reinvented version of me?
sentences.zh: 如果人们不喜欢这个重塑后的我怎么办？

sentences.en: I lose all my friends and I end up alone.
sentences.zh: 我失去了所有的朋友，最终孤独一人怎么办？

sentences.en: You know, what if, what if, what if?
sentences.zh: 你知道，“如果……怎么办，如果……怎么办，如果……怎么办”？

sentences.en: Not only are most of these very social fears, meaning that we are being guided more so by the potential opinions of others rather than the reality that we are the only one who has
sentences.zh: 这些不仅大多是社交恐惧，意味着我们更多地被他人的潜在意见所引导，而不是被我们是唯一一个必须

sentences.en: to experience and enjoy our lives, but they are also just anxious thoughts.
sentences.zh: 体验和享受我们生活的人这一事实所引导，而且它们也只是焦虑的想法。

sentences.en: They are not predictions.
sentences.zh: 它们不是预测。

sentences.en: They most likely not come true.
sentences.zh: 它们极有可能不会成真。

sentences.en: If you've listened to our most recent episode on anxiety, you'll know that the easiest way to distinguish between an anxious thought and a thought that you should pay attention to
sentences.zh: 如果你听过我们最近关于焦虑的那一集，你就会知道区分焦虑想法和你应该关注的想法的最简单方法

sentences.en: is if those thoughts begin with a what if.
sentences.zh: 就是看这些想法是否以“如果……怎么办”开头。

sentences.en: Here's how we counteract that.
sentences.zh: 我们是这样反击的。

sentences.en: We counteract it with what else or so what statements.
sentences.zh: 我们用“还有什么”或“那又怎样”的陈述来反击它。

sentences.en: So let's take this statement.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们拿这个陈述来说。

sentences.en: What if I tell everyone about my dreams and I fail?
sentences.zh: 如果我告诉所有人我的梦想却失败了怎么办？

sentences.en: You know, I'll be so embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会很尴尬的。

sentences.en: I better play it safe.
sentences.zh: 我最好还是求稳。

sentences.en: That's one way of thinking and it is a naturally limited way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思维方式，而且是一种天生受限的思维方式。

sentences.en: But consider now ending that statement with so what?
sentences.zh: 但现在考虑用“那又怎样”来结束这个陈述。

sentences.en: Okay, maybe I'll be embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我会尴尬。

sentences.en: So what?
sentences.zh: 那又怎样？

sentences.en: What is the worst case scenario?
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况是什么？

sentences.en: I'm embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我很尴尬。

sentences.en: It's uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这很不舒服。

sentences.en: So what?
sentences.zh: 那又怎样？

sentences.en: So people might not like me.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能不喜欢我。

sentences.en: So what?
sentences.zh: 那又怎样？

sentences.en: And then again, keep going.
sentences.zh: 然后再次，继续下去。

sentences.en: Keep going with the so what's until you get to the final conclusion of your fear and you realize that actually there is not much harm that embarrassment can really do.
sentences.zh: 不断追问“那又怎样”，直到你找到恐惧的最终结论，你会发现尴尬其实并不会造成多大的伤害。

sentences.en: This method is about taking an anxious fear-based thought and actually interrogating it because
sentences.zh: 这种方法是关于审视那些基于焦虑的念头，并对其进行质询，因为

sentences.en: so often we're too scared to even think about our anxious thoughts that we just let them get away with lying to us.
sentences.zh: 我们常常因为太害怕去思考焦虑的念头，以至于任由它们欺骗我们。

sentences.en: But when we say, so what?
sentences.zh: 但当我们问“那又怎样”时，

sentences.en: Our anxiety kind of is like, oh, well, you've never questioned me before.
sentences.zh: 我们的焦虑感会觉得：哦，好吧，你以前从未质疑过我。

sentences.en: So I don't really know.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实也不清楚。

sentences.en: I don't really know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And that's when I think we see things more clearly.
sentences.zh: 而就在那时，我认为我们能看得更清楚。

sentences.en: We see things for what they really are, which is not as big in reality as they are in our minds.
sentences.zh: 我们能看清事物的本质，它们在现实中远没有在我们脑海中那么严重。

sentences.en: The other option is to say, well, what else?
sentences.zh: 另一种选择是问：“还有什么可能？”

sentences.en: What if people don't like this new version of me?
sentences.zh: 如果人们不喜欢这个全新的我呢？

sentences.en: OK, that's one unlikely option.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一种不太可能的情况。

sentences.en: But what else?
sentences.zh: 但还有什么可能呢？

sentences.en: Let's expand that disaster scenario and go in search of some other alternatives.
sentences.zh: 让我们扩展一下那个灾难性的剧本，去寻找其他可能性。

sentences.en: You know, what if I actually attract people who are really aligned with who I truly am?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我吸引到的是真正与我灵魂契合的人呢？

sentences.en: What if I suddenly meet the greatest friends I'll ever have?
sentences.zh: 如果我突然遇到了我这辈子最好的朋友呢？

sentences.en: What if I suddenly attract a love that I deserve?
sentences.zh: 如果我突然吸引到了我应得的爱情呢？

sentences.en: What if I completely level up every aspect of my life and I never look back?
sentences.zh: 如果我彻底提升了生活的方方面面，从此不再回头呢？

sentences.en: What if I am the happiest I've ever been?
sentences.zh: 如果我变得前所未有的快乐呢？

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么可能？

sentences.en: Remember, the first thought that you have is probably not the most accurate.
sentences.zh: 记住，你脑海中冒出的第一个念头往往不是最准确的。

sentences.en: And you can grab onto that thought.
sentences.zh: 你可以抓住那个念头。

sentences.en: You can let it control you.
sentences.zh: 你可以任由它控制你。

sentences.en: You can let it dominate your choices.
sentences.zh: 你可以任由它主导你的选择。

sentences.en: But you also have this extreme power and ability to be whoever you want to be.
sentences.zh: 但你同样拥有巨大的力量和能力，去成为你想成为的任何人。

sentences.en: If you just zoom out and question your fear, replacing that what if with what else or so what.
sentences.zh: 只要你跳出来审视自己的恐惧，用“还有什么可能”或“那又怎样”来代替那个“如果……怎么办”。

sentences.en: During this, you know, brief time that we have on Earth, you deserve at the bare minimum to actually be yourself.
sentences.zh: 在我们在这世上短暂的时间里，你至少应该活出真实的自己。

sentences.en: Sometimes we do find ourselves in a loop of not knowing who we are, not liking who we are either, not liking our lives because of boredom, stagnation, you know, isolation.
sentences.zh: 有时我们确实会陷入一种循环：不知道自己是谁，也不喜欢现在的自己，因为无聊、停滞和孤独，也不喜欢自己的生活。

sentences.en: The longer you spend as this version of you, you will become quite used to the discomfort and you will no longer feel like you have to outgrow that shell.
sentences.zh: 你以这种状态生活得越久，就会越习惯这种不适，也就越不会觉得需要打破这层外壳。

sentences.en: You will just keep squeezing yourself back in, hiding away.
sentences.zh: 你只会不断地把自己缩回去，躲藏起来。

sentences.en: And it becomes a lot easier to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 而这种状态变得越来越容易忍受。

sentences.en: I don't want that for you.
sentences.zh: 我不希望你这样。

sentences.en: To be honest, I don't want that for anyone.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不希望任何人这样。

sentences.en: I don't want anyone to be 80 and think, what if I just done it a little bit bigger?
sentences.zh: 我不希望任何人到了80岁时想：如果我当初再勇敢一点会怎样？

sentences.en: What if I just had one six month period of reinvention?
sentences.zh: 如果我当初给自己六个月的时间去重塑自我会怎样？

sentences.en: Because you have no idea what that could do for your life.
sentences.zh: 因为你根本不知道那会对你的生活产生多大的影响。

sentences.en: You have no idea, you know, how much growth and new experiences you could have in six months.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道，在六个月里，你能获得多少成长和新体验。

sentences.en: How many weeks is that?
sentences.zh: 那是有多少周？

sentences.en: Oh my God, I've got to do quick maths, like 24 weeks.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我得快速算一下，大概24周吧。

sentences.en: I could be completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 我可能完全算错了。

sentences.en: Please correct me.
sentences.zh: 请纠正我。

sentences.en: 24 weeks, right?
sentences.zh: 24周，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You could just be a completely new person.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以变成一个全新的人。

sentences.en: That's 24 weeks of time for you to reinvent, transform, invest in yourself.
sentences.zh: 那是24周的时间，让你去重塑、去蜕变、去投资自己。

sentences.en: This is an investment.
sentences.zh: 这是一项投资。

sentences.en: I really want you to take your dreams seriously.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你能认真对待自己的梦想。

sentences.en: Take responsibility for your happiness.
sentences.zh: 为自己的幸福负责。

sentences.en: Take responsibility for evolving into the most authentic version of yourself, even if that requires a bit of a painful metamorphosis.
sentences.zh: 为进化成最真实的自己而负责，即使这需要经历一点痛苦的蜕变。

sentences.en: So I really hope that you got something from this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以我真心希望你从这一集中有所收获。

sentences.en: I hope that you can take on board this advice.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能采纳这些建议。

sentences.en: You know, you can cherry pick it as you wish.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以根据需要进行选择。

sentences.en: If some things you already do, some things you don't.
sentences.zh: 有些事你已经在做了，有些则没有。

sentences.en: Whatever you need, take what you need.
sentences.zh: 无论你需要什么，拿走你需要的部分就好。

sentences.en: That's what we always say at the end of these episodes.
